result.stdout:
Usage: tic [options] file
       tic -D
       tic -V | --version

Compile or validate terminfo source.

  -c              check source only; do not publish database entries
  -e name,...     process only selected canonical names or aliases
  -x              permit unknown extended capability names
  -o directory    publish beneath an explicit conventional database root
  -s              write a concise publication summary to standard error
      --force     replace existing compiled destinations safely
  -D              print Runtime database discovery locations and exit
  -V, --version   print the Icod.TermInfo tool-suite version and exit
      --help      display this help and exit

Use '-' as file to read strict UTF-8 source from standard input.
Unambiguous short options may be clustered; -e and -o accept attached values; use -- before a source filename beginning with '-'.
Without -o, publication uses directory-valued TERMINFO, then the Runtime-defined user database; system roots are never selected implicitly.

result.stdout:
Usage: infocmp [options] [terminal ...]
       infocmp -u [options] target parent [parent ...]
       infocmp -D
       infocmp -V | --version

Inspect one effective terminal, compare terminals semantically, or synthesize relative source.
With no terminal operand, TERM supplies the requested one-terminal name.
With two or more operands and no -u, the first is compared with each subsequent terminal.

Database selection:
  -A directory    use this explicit database for the first terminal
  -B directory    use this explicit database for subsequent terminals

Source presentation:
  -0              emit one logical source line without wrapping
  -1              emit one capability per line without continuation wrapping
  -w width        request canonical string-capability wrapping width
  -s key          order standard capabilities by d, i, l, or c

Relative synthesis:
  -u              rewrite target relative to each ordered parent using use=
  -c -u           accepted as an ncurses-compatible synonym for -u
  -x              allow required local extended declarations/cancellations

Comparison modes:
  -d              list semantic differences; default for two or more operands
  -c              list capabilities with common effective values
  -n              list standard capabilities absent from all compared entries
  -q              use shorter comparison presentation

Other options:
  -x              include effective extended capabilities where defined
  -D              print Runtime database discovery locations and exit
  -V, --version   print the Icod.TermInfo tool-suite version and exit
      --help      display this help and exit

Sort keys: d=compiled-table order, i=terminfo short name, l=long variable name, c=termcap code.
Without -x, relative synthesis fails if reproducing the target requires local extended directives.
The -n universe is the closed standard capability catalog even when -x is supplied.
Unambiguous short options may be clustered; -A, -B, -w, and -s accept attached values; use -- before a ter
[truncated]

result.stdout:
Usage: toe [options] [directory ...]
       toe -u file
       toe -U file
       toe -D
       toe -V | --version

List parsed terminal descriptions from conventional terminfo databases or analyze terminfo source dependencies.

With directory operands, inspect exactly those roots in operand order.
Without directory operands, use Runtime discovery order and inspect the first applicable conventional database.

Options:
  -a              inspect all discovered conventional databases
  -h              write a heading naming each inspected database
  -s              sort entries by canonical terminal name; with -a, mark semantic duplicates
  -u file         list forward use= dependencies in source order
  -U file         list reverse use= dependencies deterministically
  -D              print Runtime database discovery locations and exit
  -V, --version   print version information and exit
      --help      display this help and exit

Unambiguous listing options may be clustered; -u/-U accept attached source paths; use -- before a directory or source filename beginning with '-'.
